title: Discontinuous strong-to-weak symmetry breaking transition from thermal pure states
authors: Taiki Haga, Masaya Kunimi, Masaya Nakagawa
abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in many-body quantum systems undergoing decoherence from thermal pure states. For generic initial pure states with volume-law entanglement entropy, we show that the system undergoes a discontinuous dynamical phase transition at a critical time. This transition is accompanied by a singularity in the entropy of the system, which saturates to its maximum value at the same critical time. Through numerical simulations of the dephasing Ising and hard-core boson models, we establish the universality of this transition across different symmetries. Our results reveal that the dynamical emergence of a decohered mixed state from a highly entangled state is not a gradual asymptotic relaxation, but rather a sharp phase transition driven by a sudden collapse of global coherence.
summary: The research investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics of spontaneous symmetry breaking in open quantum systems undergoing decoherence. It establishes that this transition is not a smooth relaxation but a sharp dynamical phase transition occurring at a critical time $t_c$. Crucially, the authors demonstrate that macroscopic randomness in the initial state is an indispensable prerequisite for observing this discontinuous singularity.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) transition in a quantum many-body system undergoing decoherence from thermal pure states occurs gradually or via a sharp, discontinuous dynamical phase transition.
main_result: The emergence of strong-to-weak symmetry breaking is predicted to be a discontinuous dynamical phase transition at a critical time $t_c$, accompanied by singularities in global entropy and order parameters. This requires the initial state to possess volume-law entanglement (i.e., macroscopic randomness).
method: Theoretical analysis combines exact calculations of correlation functions (like R\'enyi-2 correlators) with numerical simulations of open quantum dynamics governed by Lindblad master equations.
model_or_system: The models include the dephasing transverse-field Ising model and hard-core boson systems. The dynamics are studied in the context of open quantum systems undergoing local dephasing from highly entangled initial states (e.g., Haar-random pure states).
key_observables: Fidelity correlator ($ ar{F}$), R\'enyi-2 correlator ($ ar{R}$), global entropy ($S$), and purity $P(t)$.
important_parameters: System size ($L$), dephasing rate ($\gamma$), interaction strength ($J$), transverse field ($h$). The critical time $t_c$ is a key parameter.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on self-averaging properties for typical values and utilizes mean-field approximations (single-site, two-site cluster) to capture the finite-size scaling of the transition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of $ ar{F}$ and $ ar{R}$, showing crossing points indicative of $t_c$. Finite-size scaling analysis confirms that only random/thermal states exhibit a size-independent critical time, while structured states (GHZ) show divergence.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the dynamics across different initial state types (Haar-random vs. GHZ/Dicke/Rainbow), using multiple correlation metrics ($ ar{F},  ar{R}$) and analyzing finite-size scaling to establish the necessary condition—macroscopic randomness—for a discontinuous dynamical phase transition.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, information-theoretic framework for understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, showing that the *nature* of initial entanglement (random vs. structured) dictates whether symmetry breaking happens abruptly or asymptotically.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
